Topic: The Logic of Abstract Vector Spaces

Target audience: University students (Undergraduate STEM)

Section: section_1 — Prerequisite Review: From Arrows to Rules

Lecture lines:
Vectors are arrows with length and direction.
They follow specific algebraic rules.
Addition and scaling are fundamental.

Planned animations:
Create a 2D arrow at the origin with color #FF5733 (Orange).
Animate the arrow stretching and rotating; color changes to #33FF57 (Green).
Transition the arrow into a discrete coordinate point (Dot) at (2, 3) using #3357FF (Blue).

Section: section_2 — The Generalization Leap

Lecture lines:
A vector space is a collection of objects.
It satisfies eight fundamental axioms.
Vectors aren't just physical arrows.
Functions can be vectors.
Polynomials can be vectors too.

Planned animations:
Start with the Arrow icon (Color #FF5733).
Morph Arrow icon into a Function symbol f(x) (Color #33FF57).
Morph Function symbol into a Polynomial expression ax²+bx+c (Color #3357FF).

Section: section_3 — Application: The Library of Sounds

Lecture lines:
Audio signals can be vectors.
Each time point is a dimension.
Adding clips creates a new sound.
This represents signal superposition.
Abstraction simplifies complex sound analysis.

Planned animations:
Draw a wave signal as a long vector line (Color #FF5733).
Display two signal vectors 'Bass' and 'Treble' (Colors #33FF57, #3357FF).
Animate the sum of the two vectors to create a complex waveform vector (Color #FF33FF).

Section: section_4 — Core Constraints: The Axiomatic DNA

Lecture lines:
Spaces must pass the stress test.
Closure requires staying within the set.
Sum of vectors must be inside.

Planned animations:
Create a set container for polynomials; show a Gatekeeper icon (Color #FF5733).
Show a sum operation attempt; if it stays in the set, animate Gatekeeper to open (Color #33FF57).
Show an invalid sum operation; if it leaves the set, animate Gatekeeper to stay closed (Color #FF3333).

Section: section_5 — Conclusion: The Power of Abstraction

Lecture lines:
Abstraction unifies physics and engineering.
We use familiar algebraic tools.
Data points obey these same rules.

Planned animations:
Start with a single Arrow vector (Color #FF5733).
Rapidly zoom out to reveal a vast cloud of data points (Color #3357FF).
Fade in a unified structure overlay connecting all elements (Color #FFFFFF).

from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

        self.setup_layout("Prerequisite Review: From Arrows to Rules", [

        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")

        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):

                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])

        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]

        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2

from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Conclusion: The Power of Abstraction", [
            "Abstraction unifies physics and engineering.",
            "We use familiar algebraic tools.",
            "Data points obey these same rules."
        ])
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Start with a single Arrow vector
        vector = Arrow(start=ORIGIN, end=RIGHT*1.5, color="#FF5733")
        self.place_at_grid(vector, 'C3')
        self.play(Create(vector))
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#FF5733")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Rapidly zoom out to reveal a vast cloud of data points
        dots = VGroup(*[Dot(point=np.random.uniform(-1, 1, 3), color="#3357FF") for _ in range(50)])
        self.place_in_area(dots, 'B2', 'E5', scale_factor=0.5)
        
        self.play(
            FadeOut(vector),
            Create(dots),
            run_time=2
        )
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#3357FF")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Fade in a unified structure overlay
        overlay = VGroup(*[Line(dots[i].get_center(), dots[(i+1)%50].get_center(), color=WHITE, stroke_width=1) for i in range(50)])
        self.add(overlay)
        self.play(FadeIn(overlay))
        self.lecture[2].set_color(WHITE)
